questions.question: Which asset class historically exhibits the highest annual price volatility and drawdown risk?
options: Treasury Bills
Equity Shares (Stocks)
Sovereign Gold Bonds
Dated Government Bonds
questions.explanation: Equity shares represent residual business claims and historically experience higher annual price fluctuations and drawdown cycles.

questions.question: Why might an investor with a 100% stock portfolio consider adding REITs, InvITs, or Bonds?
options: To eliminate all taxes completely
To introduce predictable cash distributions and reduce total portfolio drawdown during stock market downswings
Because SEBI makes holding other assets mandatory
To guarantee 50% compounding every year
questions.explanation: Diversification across uncorrelated income-generating assets provides recurring cash flows and reduces overall portfolio volatility.

questions.question: Can you hold stocks, REITs, G-Secs, and corporate bonds in the same single Demat account?
options: No, every asset class requires a completely separate demat account
Yes, an NSDL or CDSL Demat account holds all eligible electronic securities under a single BO ID
Only if your net worth exceeds ₹10 crore
Only during trading festival hours
questions.explanation: Indian central depositories (NSDL and CDSL) hold all asset classes in one consolidated 16-digit Beneficiary Owner ID.

questions.question: What is 'Yield to Maturity' (YTM) and why is it not applicable to common equity shares?
options: YTM applies only to gold
YTM calculates the annualized return of a debt bond with fixed maturity and coupons; equities have no fixed maturity date or fixed contractual payouts
Equities have a negative YTM by law
YTM is a trading fee charged by stockbrokers
questions.explanation: YTM requires fixed contractual future cash flows and an explicit maturity date, which equities do not possess.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between REIT cash distributions and corporate stock dividends?
options: REITs are legally required to distribute at least 90% of NDCF; equity companies pay dividends entirely at management discretion
REITs pay interest in cash, while stocks only pay bonus shares
Stock dividends are completely tax-free up to ₹1 crore
There is no difference
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates REITs distribute 90%+ of net distributable cash, whereas standard corporations can retain 100% of profits without paying dividends.
